study_type_evidence.quote: A single dose of leuprolide and LOC was administered subcutaneously to male SD rats.

in_vivo_species.quote: Rats underwent surgical implantation of a cannula in the femoral artery under anesthesia

agents.name: Leuprolide
agents.sequence_source: The body names the drug leuprolide but does not print a sequence; PEPlife2's string uses pGlu for pyroglutamate and lowercase l for D-Leu.
agents.dose_route_quote: Different leuprolide formulations (Lorelin injection® and LOC) were subcutaneously injected at doses of 0.1 mg/kg for leuprolide
agents.pk_quote: the half-life of drug elimination—at the terminal phase (t1/2)—was 38.2 ± 4.3 and 172 ± 66 min for leuprolide and the LOC, respectively, after subcutaneous administration

agents.name: LOC (leuprolide-oleic acid conjugate)
agents.sequence_source: PEPlife2's string for LOC is leuprolide MINUS its N-terminal pGlu, and does not encode the oleic acid at all - so the conjugate is represented as a TRUNCATION of the parent rather than an extension of it.
agents.dose_route_quote: 0.122 mg/kg (0.1 mg/kg as leuprolide) for the LOC into rats

bioanalytical_quote: The validated UPLC-MS/MS method was successfully applied to compare the pharmacokinetic behaviors of unmodified leuprolide and the leuprolide-fatty acid conjugate in rat plasma.
notes: Two of three PEPlife2 values verified directly in the body: leuprolide 38.2 ± 4.3 min and LOC 172 ± 66 min. The third, 166 ± 38 min, is Table 3's value for LEUPROLIDE MEASURED AS A METABOLITE after LOC dosing (Figure 4), and PEPlife2 labels its Test Sample accordingly. That third record needs care: it is not leuprolide's own half-life - the body measures that as 38.2 min - but the apparent half-life of leuprolide released from the conjugate, which is formation-rate-limited by LOC hydrolysis and therefore tracks LOC's 172 min. Filed against the leuprolide sequence it asserts a 4.3-fold longer half-life for the same molecule. SEQUENCE DEFECT: PEPlife2 gives LOC the string HWSYlLRP while giving leuprolide pGlu-HWSYlLRP. The conjugate is leuprolide PLUS oleic acid, so its string should extend the parent's, not drop the N-terminal pyroglutamate; the oleic acid is not encoded at all. As written the conjugate looks like a truncation of the parent while carrying a 4.5-fold longer half-life. The lowercase l marks D-Leu, which the training-set cleaner upper-cases, losing the stereochemistry.
